Being located across a small road from the beach, and a short trike ride to D'Mall, was a blessing as you will get a good night's sleep. We enjoyed a swim in the pool before going to bed. There's plenty of restaurants and bars within walking distance, even a large amusement park and Go Karts you ride up for a fantastic 360 degree panoramic view of the island. The resort will also take you to Arials Point in their large boat where you can jump into the sea off jumping boards between 3 and 15 metres above the sea. I suggest you wear sandshoes for walking on rocks, and you will get wet getting on and off the boat. The all day trip included drinks and BBQ lunch.
I love that they have provided a Balcony for smokers and its on the roof deck thus giving you a nice beachfront view and a romantic setting at night.

review_text: 2014년 2월에 이 리조트에 다녀왔습니다. 이번에 세부 세번째이고 그동안 풀크라, 크림슨을 갔었습니다, 샹크릴라 리조트는 많은 사람에 비해 식당은 매우 좁아 식사는 항상 전쟁이었고, 오믈릿 주문에 요리사 눈치를 보아야 했고, 호텔 자체가 많은 사람을 수용할 시스템을 갖추지 못하였습니다. 우리가족 9명이 예약을 하였고, 체크인도 9명이 했는데 체크인 다음날 점심 식사하는데 갑자기 8명 예약되었다고 식사 차지를 하겠다는데 황당하였습니다. 그에 대한 한국 직원의 지원도 미비하였습니다. 수영장은 어린아이들을 데려가기 부담스럽습니다. 크림슨의 경우 안전요원이 아이들과 같이 놀아주는 친절과 배려가 있는 반면, 이 호텔의 안전요원은 엄마아빠에게 아이와 같이 있을 것을 강요하고 감시할 뿐이어서 상전같이 느껴졌습니다.  또한 체크아웃할때는 쓴 금액보다 많이 청구되는 경우가 많아 이를 정정하는데 시간이 많이 필요합니다. 따라서 체크아웃시 넉넉한 시간이 필요하고 모든 지불에 꼭 영수증을 챙기는 것이 필요합니다. 음식도 별루고, 객실도 청결하지 못하였습니다. 다만 좋은 점은 괜찮은 해변을 갖고 있다는 것.

I've got mixed feelings about Manila Ocean Park, thus the 3-star rating.  The aquarium (Oceanarium) part of the park was fun. It's not necessarily "world-class" quality, but it's pretty decent. My family had fun looking at all the fish and other sea creatures. For the price, it was somewhat small, but not too bad. Definitely more of a vacation price, not a "visit every day" price, but that's expected for a place like this.  We didn't get a chance to see most of the attractions at the park, but in addition to the Oceanarium, we did go through the exhibit Trails to Antarctica. property: Best Western Hotel La Corona Manila
review_text: Booked the Best Western with my wife returning from Mindoro Oriental. The location is almost in the middle of the old red light district and our friends who came to pick us up were shocked.  I was not that bothered as it was meant to be just a short night. However, when we came back to hotel after dinner we found that the window was open and it could not be closed fully as a hinge was deformed and out of position.  The scratches on the frame showed it had been pushed repeatedly and it was like this for weeks if not months. Even after we called someone to check it they could not fully close it as it was hanging sideways.  The window on room 411 opens to the road where bars run all night. The music was not allowing us to sleep and at 2am my wife had to go to reception to complain as the reception would not answer.  Their response on our request to get another room was a pair of ear plugs.  It seems like the place has become the haunt of business people who frequent the seedy local bars and don't care about noise after one too many. Don't be surprised if you find your partner, husband or other half had been here many times before.  After their lack of interest and the answer that they don't have a method to monitor complaints, we decided we would not get back to Best Western again.  It seems silly now to point that the bar did not have light drinks or that shampoo was present but not shower gel or that there are hardly any power points other than one free next to the bed.  If you have to come here just make sure you avoid 411 and ask for a room not on the road of you want to sleep.  There are many good hotels in Manila and there is no reason to take this.

I learned about Karl through Scubaboard when I was looking into getting into technical diving.  But it didn’t pan out so I took the Sidemount course for the time being.  I took my advanced Sidemount course with Karl at the period when Manila Dive Academy was just coming into being.  It started with e-mails then an actual meeting to cover the theoretical bits. From the get go I was impressed with MDA.  They are very professional, safety conscious and helpful.  Karl did not get tired of answering my queries be it about the course or other SCUBA matters which are not really related to the course.  I have a leaning towards the DIR side of the spectrum and was very happy that they also adapted the same principles but are not rigid about it (flame suit on :-)). I did the checkout dives in two successive weekends. The weather was bad during the first weekend so we had to abort the dives. They are very safety conscious and taught at the pace of the student. I did not feel like I was being hurried along the familiar “certification pipeline”.  Equipment was topnotch (they have their own set and not the generic resort rental).  But what really sets them apart are the instructors who I believe are doing this more as a hobby.  They also do not confine themselves to the basic course requirements but incorporate lessons that they learned from personal experience and other courses that they teach. But your relationship with MDA does not end with certification. You are welcome to dive with them after. (I would be diving with them more often if I had the time). As a final word I am so happy with their service that I will be pursuing further training with MDA this coming year.

Real italian food from a real italian, Daniele Bellini. Whenever we eat there, we usually start with the delicious caprese, along with the focaccia, and maybe followed by the fabulous Grilled Porcini Salad. Lately, we've been favoring the fresh Truffle Cream Ravioli, Risotto al Funghi, Quattro Formaggi pizza for the kids, and if we're in the mood for dessert, we finish everything with some gelato. Other pastas are quite good too, and the steaks and shrimp are also great. Frequent visitors might want to ask for what they have off-menu, and may be gifted with some surprise treats.  Parking is a weak point for Daniele's, and the ambience is not as flashy as other places, but the service is quite warm, and prices are quite cheap, considering this is a true italian experience.  The outside appearance of Daniele's may not be very inviting, but give it a chance, and I'm sure you won't be disappointed.

First off, when you arrive at the airport, don't go to the people yelling "Taxi".  They'll want 20-30 dollars American for the ride.  They'll even have a laminated price card to show you.  Instead, look for the actual small (Toyota Corolla) cabs and pay by the meter.  The actual ride should only cost about 100 pesos (a little over 2 dollars).  International flights should exit the airport on the west side and the hotel will be on its east side.  Now for the Hotel, security is tight.  Which is good.  They search you and have a K9 to sniff the bags before each and every entry.  The elevator only works when you put your room key in it for extra security.  Please note that the entire compound of hotels and attractions is surrounded by a pretty ghetto area.  The actual city of Manilla is about 10 clicks away.  Check in was fine.  I arrived late night so didn't have any lines to deal with.  I paid through Hotels.com.  I didn't need my credit card or have to leave a cash deposit on the room but you might if you're staying for longer.  I just handed them my passport and they took care of the rest.    The hallways aren't air conditioned.  Some vending machines on each floor.  2 Queen bed room (the least expensive):  No carpets in the room.  A small flat screen.  One standard electronic room safe.  They give you 2 bottles of water, 2 bars of soap, 2 surprisingly decent toothbrushes (saved one to use on the plane), 2 mini tubes of Colgate toothpaste, 2 towels, 2 plastic cups and 2 pairs of disposable slippers.  A/C has decent power but you can only choose between on and off.  Regular toilet but no bath tub.  Just a stand up shower with a curtain. Smoking rooms are optional.  Wifi signal was weak.  Will only let you sign one device in (they give you a log in name and password).  Directly across from the entrance is a huge construction project that looks like it just began (March 2014) so if you're a light sleeper, request a room not facing the front.  McDonalds is next door (24/7) and the casino is across the small street from there.  Casino was alright.  You're allowed to smoke.  Not allowed to tip.  The general area has tables of about 100 to 300 peso minimums 5000-10000 peso maximums.  A lot of slot machines (about half the casino).  24/7.  I slept through the free breakfast.  Checked out right at noon.  Everyone else seemed to be checked out already so I skipped that line too.  Handed the girl my keycards and only had to wait 1 minute for her to say I was checked out.  Overall, okay hotel.   The actual city of Manilla is 10 clicks away so only good as a layover Hotel.  Rooms could be better.  They were adequately clean.  Skip the free bus to the airport.  Get your own air conditioned cab out front.  Should only be about 100 pesos.  550 (12.50 American) per person airport fee when leaving the country as well.  They won't make change so make sure you visit the change counter inside the terminal or have the correct change ready.  Would stay again if I had a one day layover.  Would find one in actual Manilla if I was going as a tourist.
